text:
Alex: heads-up — last two hours we've seen p99 spikes on eu-west pools, only for jobs with high interop RDMA usage. p95 is fine, but p99 up from 420ms -> 1.8s.
Priya: noticed that too. patterns look like heavy PCIe link utilization during KV-cache warmups, plus small bursts of DMA on the NIC.
Jamie: can you paste the query id or job id? I want to correlate with tenant routing.
Alex: job ids 0x7f3a... and 0x9c2b..., dashboard: https://internal-metrics/redwood/eu-west/pcie#ad-hoc (private). both jobs on shared-gpu pools, both 8xA100 slices.
Marta: adding a note — both tenants have mixed realtime batching + frequent small file transfers (model snapshotting). That combination is a classic PCIe root contention case.
Lee: ops-bot ran the node-level probe at 15:12, attached logs show PCIe link down/up flapping on one host (host-az3-gpu-17). ops-bot: "pci_probe: link_util=92%, dma_qdepth=128, rx_drop=3"
ops-bot: system message — automated mitigation applied: moved one offending slice to warm pool, throttled snapshot IO for 2m.
Ben: results? did tail latency recover after the move?
Alex: partial improvement. p99 dropped to ~820ms but still double baseline. saw NVLINK counters spike too which implies cross-GPU NVLINK congestion after offload.
Priya: hypothesis: noisy tenant doing concurrent small mmap() + cudaMemcpyAsync patterns creating many small DMA transactions, overwhelming PCIe requestor arbitration. With MIG slices, we still share root complex so noisy neighbor wins.
Jamie: agree. long-term options: 1) dedicated physical pools for heavy RDMA/IO tenants (higher $), 2) PCIe-aware routing that prefers colocated NVLINK-only hosts for such tenants, 3) per-tenant IO shaping via cgroups/ebpf (hard).
Marta: cost tradeoffs are important — how many tenants would need dedicated pools to justify? rough calc: one noisy tenant = 0.6% cluster degradation but 3 tenants like this => noticeable SLA risks.
Lee: quick experiment suggestion: create a soft-affinity tag `pcie-sensitive` and route any job with snapshotting or mmap+cudaBurst patterns to a lower-density rack for 24h. we can set routing rule in router-config:

```
route-conditions:
  - match: workload.annotations.pcie_sensitive == "true"
    target: low_density_rack_eu_west
    priority: 60
```

Priya: also propose enabling per-tenant dma_qos throttle on host kernel for a week as we monitor. there's a small patch: `tc_qos_dma` we can enable via sysctl on candidate hosts.
Ben: ops side — is it safe to flip on dma_qos in prod? any kernel regressions?
Marta: ops-qa ran smoke last week on canary hosts, no regressions observed. still need a rollback plan.
Jamie: i'd rather try routing + IO throttle before offering dedicated pools. cheaper and reversible. can infra create a canary of 8 hosts with the routing rule + dma_qos enabled?
Lee: yes, can spin up canary slice set in eu-west-3. I'll label hosts `pcie-canary-1..8` and add router rule.
Alex: timeline? this week would be ideal since tenant traffic repeats weekdays.
Lee: I can do it tomorrow morning 06:00 UTC, will keep 2h maintenance window and rollback knob.
ops-bot: scheduled — route update + sysctl enable on hosts pcie-canary-1..8 at 2026-03-19T06:00Z (runbook #4821).
Priya: i'll add telemetry dashboards for NVLINK/PCIe per-host p99 and dma_qdepth. link to patch: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pcie-qos/pull/42
Ben: please capture cost delta for extra low-density rack capacity — ops finance needs a number if this becomes permanent.
Marta: i'll model both scenarios: route+throttle vs dedicated reserved pools and share numbers in #finance by Friday.
Alex: thanks all — keeping this thread for the experiment logs and outcome. ping me if you see p99 > 1s after the canary goes live. :thumbsup:
